title: Introduce cost-presets-as-code CLI, quant-profile diff linter, and unit-econ validation
author: Leah Mercado
description:
Motivation: Provide an auditable, reviewable 'presets-as-code' workflow for unit-economics driven defaults (batching, cache, and quantization) and a small CLI + linter to validate changes before rollout. This PR introduces a lightweight YAML schema for cost presets, a redwood CLI subcommand to validate/apply/dry-run presets, and a quant-profile diff linter that flags risk patterns (e.g. mixed-int8 on embedding heads, mismatched KV cache formats) and suggests safe fallback profiles.

Changes included (high level): - New schema: configs/cost-presets/v1/preset-schema.yaml (human readable, opinionated defaults and validation rules). - CLI: cli/redwood_cost/presets.py (commands: validate, diff, apply, dry-run). - Quant linter: tools/quant_diff.py + rules/risk_rules.yaml (identifies unsafe quant combos & latency-risk markers). - Runtime integration: runtime/config/preset_loader.cpp (safe merge of presets into runtime settings with stable defaults), runtime/batcher/preset_adapter.go (interprets batch/cache targets), and a small compatibility shim for legacy tenant defaults. - Tests: tests/unit/test_presets_validation.py, tests/integration/test_quant_linter_end_to_end.py. - Docs: docs/cost-presets-as-code.md and examples in examples/cost-presets/sample-presets.yaml.

Why this is different: Existing autotuners and heuristics adjust defaults at runtime; this change surfaces curated defaults in code reviews, provides a deterministic dry-run simulator to measure unit-econ impact, and prevents accidental risky quant rollouts via a linting gate. The goal is enabling safe, auditable operator workflows that integrate with CI and Linear/Jira.

Compatibility and rollout plan: The default behavior is opt-in. On install, the runtime still honors existing tenant-level defaults unless a preset is applied. The CLI supports a --dry-run mode that runs the simulator and emits expected token-cost delta and estimated p95 latency delta so operators can review. A small feature flag (runtime.flags.enable_preset_loader) gates the runtime merge behavior. Rollout: 1) Merge and smoke test on staging; 2) Land a small sample preset repo for internal teams; 3) Add lint gate to CI for redwood-maintained presets; 4) Gradual enable for Dedicated customers via feature flag.

Checklist: - [x] Schema and CLI implementation - [x] Unit tests for validation rules - [x] Integration test for quant diff linter - [x] Docs and example presets - [x] CI jobs added for presets lint and dry-run simulator

Risk notes: Linter is conservative by design; some safe but experimental quant combos will be flagged and require an explicit override. The runtime shim performs non-destructive merges and logs any skipped fields for auditability.
